title: $q$-th moment decomposition along the last coordinate
statement:
Let $q$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function. Write $g$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $h$ for the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, both Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then the $q$-th moment of $f$ under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ decomposes as
\[
  \E[f^q] \;=\; \E\!\left[\frac{(g+h)^q + (g-h)^q}{2}\right],
\]
where the expectation on the right is taken over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables
$g$ is the average of $f$ over its last coordinate
$h$ is the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate
replaced:
For $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, writing $g = \mathrm{avgLast}\,f$ and
$h = \mathrm{diffLast}\,f$, the $q$-th moment decomposes as
\[
  \E[f^q] = \E\!\left[\frac{(g+h)^q + (g-h)^q}{2}\right].
\]
